hub.title: Nostalgia: 80s, 90s and 2000s Snacks, Consoles and Gadgets
hub.description: What was a pager, a Famicom, a Tamagotchi or Y2K? {n} things from 1980s–2000s childhoods: what they were, what they cost, what happened to them and whether you can still get them.
hub.lede: Snacks, game consoles, Walkmans and pagers, marbles and playground games, early internet and Chinese childhood classics. One thing per page: what it was, when it was around, what it cost, what became of it and whether it still exists.
about: Every page answers "what was it?" in a sentence or two, then covers when it was popular, what it looked like and cost, why it was discontinued or replaced, and whether you can still get it today.
Entries were picked from what people actually search for. Dates, prices and status are checked against Wikipedia, company pages and news reports; where nobody knows for sure, the page says so.

faq.q: What does the nostalgia section cover?
faq.a: Things many people used, ate or played with as children from the 1980s to the 2000s: snacks and drinks, game consoles, gadgets like the Walkman and pager, playground games, the early internet, and everyday life in China such as ration coupons and corner shops.

faq.q: What does "status" mean on a page?
faq.a: It is where the product stands now: still sold, brought back as a re-release, or discontinued, as of the page's update date. Games, activities and places have no status.

faq.q: Can I buy these things here?
faq.a: No. cv.cm sells nothing and recommends no shops; pages only say whether something is still made or has an official re-release.
